group.passage: In Japan, a gift sometimes arrives wrapped not in paper but in a square piece of cloth. This cloth, called a furoshiki, is a jack of all trades: it can hold a lunch box, a bottle of water, a pile of books, or a present for a friend. When the job is done, the cloth is simply opened, folded, and kept for next time. The habit of wrapping things in cloth has deep roots in Japan. It is said to go back to the Nara period, more than a thousand years ago, when valuable objects were wrapped in cloth to keep them safe. The name furoshiki, however, comes from the Edo period, which lasted from 1603 to 1867. In Japanese, "furo" means bath, while "shiki" means to spread. At that time, many people went to large public baths. Before bathing, they wrapped their clothes and other things in a cloth so that their belongings would not get mixed up with those of other people. The cloth was useful outside the bath, too. People going on long journeys packed what they needed into big cloth bundles and carried them on their backs. Many old Japanese prints show travelers walking along roads with such bundles. Over time, all wrapping cloths of this kind came to be known by the same name. The cloth found a new role in 2006, when Yuriko Koike, then Japan's Minister of the Environment, designed a special one made from recycled plastic bottles. It was decorated with birds and flowers painted by Ito Jakuchu, an artist of the Edo period. She hoped people would carry their shopping in cloth rather than in plastic or paper bags. The Japanese have a word for the feeling she wanted to share: "mottainai," which means something like "What a waste!"

translation_zh.text:
在日本，禮物有時候不是用紙包，而是用一塊方形的布包著送來。這塊布叫做「風呂敷」，它什麼都能做：可以包便當、一瓶水、一疊書，或是送朋友的禮物。用完之後，只要把布打開、摺好，留到下次再用就好。
用布包東西的習慣在日本有很深的根源。據說它可以追溯到一千多年前的奈良時代，當時貴重的物品會用布包起來保護。不過，「風呂敷」這個名稱來自江戶時代，也就是 1603 年到 1867 年。在日文裡，「風呂」是洗澡，「敷」是鋪開的意思。那時候，許多人會去大型的公共澡堂。洗澡前，他們用一塊布把衣服和其他東西包起來，這樣自己的東西才不會和別人的混在一起。
這塊布在澡堂外也很有用。出遠門的人把需要的東西裝進大布包，背在背上。許多日本的古老版畫都畫著背著這種布包、走在路上的旅人。久而久之，這一類的包袱布都被叫做同一個名稱。
2006 年，這塊布找到了新的角色：當時的日本環境大臣小池百合子，設計了一條用回收塑膠瓶做成的特別布巾。上面的花鳥圖案是江戶時代的畫家伊藤若冲所畫。她希望人們用布來裝買的東西，而不要用塑膠袋或紙袋。日本人有一個字可以表達她想傳達的感受：「もったいない」，意思大約是「真浪費！」
